lessons.title: When criticism feels like an attack
lessons.teach: Follow the conversation one message at a time. Notice what the behaviour might be achieving before you decide why it happened. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Distinguish observable evidence from a tentative explanation of everyday self-focus versus a persistent trait.

nodes.title: What might be happening?
nodes.body:
In some narcissistic difficulties, a person's sense of worth depends heavily on recognition. A correction can then feel like a broader verdict on competence. Dismissing another person's contribution may offer brief relief while making the relationship more adversarial. This is a tentative self-esteem regulation account, not a diagnosis.

Deliberate career advantage and emotional defensiveness can coexist. The wider, enduring pattern matters far more than a single argument.
nodes.sources: Pincus et al. (2009), Pathological Narcissism Inventory; DSM-5-TR, personality functioning.

nodes.title: Try a different response
nodes.prompt: The goal is to improve the situation without pretending that you can read the person's mind.
nodes.explanation: A proportionate response deals with the actual situation: We can accurately credit your leadership and the analysis I completed before the slide is sent. Its value does not depend on the other person accepting an interpretation of their motives.
nodes.counterexample: Some situations require independent support or safer channels rather than another direct conversation. Deliberate career advantage and emotional defensiveness can coexist. The wider, enduring pattern matters far more than a single argument.
nodes.sources: Pincus et al. (2009), Pathological Narcissism Inventory; DSM-5-TR, personality functioning.

lessons.title: What would change your mind?
lessons.teach: An initial explanation is useful only if it can be challenged. Revisit the characters, test a rival account and apply the idea in another setting. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Test an account of everyday self-focus versus a persistent trait with new evidence and transfer it to a new case.
